summary.text: You won the ball in the attacking third 49 times (1.3 a match). 20% became a shot within 10s, worth 0.025 xG per regain: about the league average for that {unit}.

summary.title: Most productive regain zones
summary.text: Winning it here is most likely to end in a chance. D2 (left-centre, opposition half): 9% of 35 regains led to a shot within 10s, worth 0.023 xG each (2.6x the league average for that zone, though within normal variation); D4 (right wing, opposition half): 14% of 56 regains led to a shot within 10s, worth 0.019 xG each (4.0x the league average for that zone, though within normal variation).

summary.title: Least productive regain zones
summary.text: You win the ball here but get less from it than the average side does. Worth reviewing what happens next: first pass, support runners. D3 (right-centre, opposition half): 9% of 32 regains led to a shot within 10s, 0.5x the league return, a gap small enough to be noise; C2 (left-centre, own half): 2% of 109 regains led to a shot within 10s, 0.6x the league return, a gap small enough to be noise.

summary.title: Biggest vulnerability
summary.text: Losing the ball in D4 (right wing, opposition half) cost the most: 99 turnovers, 3% led to an opposition shot within 10s, 0.9 xG conceded across the season (1 goal). Rest-defence cover behind this area is the first thing to check.

summary.title: Read with care
summary.text: These are associations over 38 matches, not proof that pressing in a zone causes shots. Zones with fewer than 30 turnovers are hatched on the map and left out of these notes.
